name: DEMO, never a benchmark: a SPARC rotation-curve table (one galaxy's rotmod file and its Table1 row) checked against the claims of rotation-curve-sparc@0.1.0, with its free choices on a choice ledger (engine 0.5.0). (C1) the observed curve is flat within 10 km/s beyond 10 kpc; (C2) the observed velocity exceeds the baryonic one by at least 30 km/s at every row beyond 10 kpc, at the stellar mass-to-light ratios UPS_DISK and UPS_BUL; (C3) the published V_flat replays from the rows, by the procedure VF_ALGORITHM names, within 1 km/s; (C4) inside the data, the flat-curve model's mass at the last row is within 15% of the observed curve's; (C5) past the data, the flat-curve model's mass at twice the last radius, which the engine reports as counsel, never as a verdict. Every number the checks depend on that the table does not fix is a choice slot: stated by the document with a quoted span, or supplied, and named.

sources.SPARC-PAPER: Lelli, McGaugh & Schombert 2016, AJ 152, 157, https://doi.org/10.3847/0004-6256/152/6/157 (arXiv:1606.09251v1, PDF sha256 d089215877213661e40965543ee7e05736619082ad16d95e65ec059029588c63): eq. (2) for V_bar; Sect. 5.3.1 (page 9) for the mass-to-light ratios the mass models adopt, quoted from a pdftotext 4.00 -enc UTF-8 extraction of that PDF (sha256 b5f5912b3341fff6fedd7eaa44424eac443fb9e4d9fc8905415c88393f460a9d), which drops the solar-unit glyphs

sources.SPARC-TABLE1: https://astroweb.case.edu/SPARC/SPARC_Lelli2016c.mrt (sha256 5aa0501f6b0d881fa579030e315e7b5b6ef561a5bd3a07472f9929c7e5728243). Its byte-by-byte description declares 113-byte rows and its rows are 131 bytes, so it is read by splitting on whitespace, a stated narrowing
sources.SPARC-TABLE2: https://astroweb.case.edu/SPARC/MassModels_Lelli2016c.mrt (sha256 9108994b12cc401b94a1768beca61c53ec354779385c9c9cc571049f3043244c), Note (3): Vdisk and Vbul are given for M/L = 1 solMass/solLum at [3.6]
sources.GM-SUN: IAU 2015 Resolution B3, nominal solar mass parameter GM_sun = 1.3271244e20 m^3 s^-2; with 1 kpc = 3.0856775814913673e19 m, G M_sun = 4.30091727e-6 kpc (km/s)^2, the value astropy.constants gives

choices.name: the stellar mass-to-light ratio of the disk at 3.6 um (M_sun/L_sun), which scales Vdisk in V_bar (C2)

default.source: SPARC-PAPER Sect. 5.3.1 (page 9): the mass models adopt a disk mass-to-light ratio of 0.5

choices.name: the stellar mass-to-light ratio of the bulge at 3.6 um (M_sun/L_sun), which scales Vbul in V_bar (C2)

default.source: SPARC-PAPER Sect. 5.3.1 (page 9): the mass models adopt a bulge mass-to-light ratio of 0.7

choices.name: the procedure that turns the rows into V_f (C3, FLAT_PART_ROWS, C4, C5)

default.source: SPARC-BTFR Sect. 2.2, the procedure SPARC's Table1 V_flat comes from, pinned in this build as sparc.vflat@1

choices.name: the form of the curve past its rows: flat at V_f (C4 tests it inside the data; C5 uses it past the data)

default.source: supplied by this ruleset: the simplest form the flat part suggests; SPARC states no form for the curve beyond its last row

choices.name: G M_sun in kpc (km/s)^2, which turns V^2 R into a mass in M_sun (C5)

default.source: GM-SUN: IAU 2015 nominal GM_sun in kpc (km/s)^2, as astropy.constants gives it; the document states no constant

choices.not_applicable: SPARC's rotmod rows carry no per-value quality flag. Table1's per-galaxy quality flag Q (1 to 3) is a selection criterion, not a per-value flag, and this per-galaxy demo does not read it

GALAXY.term: the galaxy the rotmod file is for (its file name) [SPARC-ROTMOD]

GALAXY_T1.term: the galaxy of the Table1 row read (Galaxy) [SPARC-TABLE1]

UNIT_RAD.term: the unit of Rad, as the rotmod header's unit line prints it [SPARC-ROTMOD]

UNIT_VOBS.term: the unit of Vobs, as the rotmod header's unit line prints it [SPARC-ROTMOD]

UNIT_VBAR_COLS.term: the one unit Vgas, Vdisk and Vbul share; reported only when the three agree [SPARC-ROTMOD]

DIST_ROTMOD.term: the distance on the rotmod header line "# Distance = ... Mpc" [SPARC-ROTMOD]

VFLAT_T1.term: Table1 Vflat, the published flat velocity (km/s) [SPARC-TABLE1]

VGAS.term: Vgas, the gas contribution including helium (km/s); may be negative [SPARC-ROTMOD, SPARC-TABLE2]

VDISK.term: Vdisk, the stellar disk contribution at M/L = 1 (km/s) [SPARC-TABLE2 Note 3]

VBUL.term: Vbul, the bulge contribution at M/L = 1 (km/s) [SPARC-TABLE2 Note 3]

line_computed.VBAR: sqrt(abs(VGAS) * VGAS + doc.UPS_DISK * abs(VDISK) * VDISK + doc.UPS_BUL * abs(VBUL) * VBUL)

checks.name: The rotmod file and the Table1 row are for the same galaxy [SPARC-ROTMOD, SPARC-TABLE1]
Vgas, Vdisk and Vbul are in km/s [SPARC-ROTMOD]
The rotmod distance equals Table1 D: the mass-model columns scale with distance, so a difference means the two tables describe different models [SPARC-ROTMOD, SPARC-TABLE1]
Rad does not decrease from the row before
Rad differs from the row before (with RAD_INCREASING: strictly increasing, so the outermost rows are the last)
At least 5 rows lie at Rad >= 10 kpc, so no single row decides C1 or C2
C1: every row at Rad >= 10 kpc lies within 10 km/s of the median Vobs of those rows (left: the largest deviation)
C1, per row, against the published value: each row at Rad >= 10 kpc lies within 10 km/s of Table1 Vflat [SPARC-TABLE1]

C2: at every row with Rad >= 10 kpc, Vobs - V_bar >= 30 km/s, V_bar = sqrt(|Vgas|Vgas + UPS_DISK |Vdisk|Vdisk + UPS_BUL |Vbul|Vbul) (left: the smallest excess) [SPARC-PAPER eq. (2), Sect. 5.3.1; SPARC-TABLE2 Note 3]
C3: V_f recomputed from the rows by the procedure VF_ALGORITHM names equals the published Table1 Vflat within 1 km/s [SPARC-BTFR Sect. 2.2, SPARC-TABLE1]
Every row from the innermost row the algorithm included outward lies within 10 km/s of the recomputed V_f
C4 (model, inside the data): at the last measured radius the flat-curve model's enclosed mass, V_f^2 R / G, lies within 15% of the observed curve's, V_obs^2 R / G (left: |ratio - 1|)

C5 (model, past the data): the flat-curve model's enclosed mass at twice the last measured radius, V_f^2 (2 R_last) / G, is at least 4e11 M_sun (left: the mass in 1e10 M_sun). It lies past the measured support, so the engine reports it as counsel
